answer: Agents must forge a verifiable work bond before trading: each identity stakes tokens and publishes a signed history of completed tasks. New identities start in a narrow canyon of low trust, able to handle only small jobs, while reputation flows like a river only after peers attest real deliveries. Creating thousands of fake agents therefore costs repeated stakes and real work, and any fraud burns the stake and resets trust to zero, so a Sybil swarm cannot cheaply outvote honest agents.
